questions.question: What does `self` refer to inside an instance method?
options: The current instance.
The parent class only.
The Python interpreter.
A global variable.
questions.explanation: `self` is the object on which the method is called.

questions.question: What does `__init__` typically do?
options: Destroy objects that are no longer used.
Initialize instance attributes for a newly created object.
Define all class methods automatically.
Make methods static by default.

questions.question: What is the difference between class variables and instance variables?
options: They are exactly the same in behavior.
Instance variables are shared; class variables are private.
Class variables are shared; instance variables belong to each object.
Class variables only work in dataclasses.
questions.explanation: Shared versus per-instance state is a core OOP distinction.

questions.question: When should you usually prefer composition?
options: Only for global state containers.
Never; inheritance is always cleaner.
Only when classes have no methods.
When you can combine smaller objects instead of forcing inheritance hierarchy.
questions.explanation: Composition is often simpler and more flexible than deep inheritance.

questions.question: What problem appears if you accidentally use a class variable for per-user state?
options: One instance change can affect all instances unexpectedly.
Python refuses to run the class.
Methods become static automatically.
The variable becomes immutable.
questions.explanation: Shared class state can leak across objects.

questions.question: What is a good use case for a dataclass?
options: Any class that must use inheritance.
A structured data model with many fields and simple behavior.
Replacing every function with a class.
Code that never stores state.
questions.explanation: Dataclasses reduce boilerplate for data-centric classes.

questions.question: What happens if you forget `self` in an instance method signature?
options: The method becomes a class method.
Python adds it automatically in every case.
Method calls usually fail with argument mismatch errors.
Nothing; it still works as intended.
questions.explanation: Python passes the instance as first argument, so the signature must account for it.

questions.question: What is the strongest sign that a class is poorly designed?
options: It contains private helper methods.
It has an __init__ method.
It uses type hints.
It handles many unrelated responsibilities.
questions.explanation: Single-responsibility design improves readability and maintainability.
